new_statements.quote: Os Xavantes repellem a poligamia, e não empregam suas armas contra o homem. Quando quazi todas as palavras de vocabulario dos Caiuás e dos Coroados terminam por silabas agudas, as dos xavantes têm quazi todas o acento agudo na penultima. Resta-me aprezentar um rezumido vocabulario comparado d'essas trez linguas, com os termos correspondentes do guarani e do portuguez.
new_statements.translation: The Xavantes reject polygamy and do not use their weapons against man. Whereas almost all the words of the vocabulary of the Caiuás [Kaiowá Guarani] and of the Coroados [Kaingang] end in stressed (oxytone) syllables, those of the Xavantes [= Oti] almost all have the acute accent [stress] on the penultimate. It remains for me to present a brief comparative vocabulary of these three languages, with the corresponding Guarani and Portuguese terms.
new_statements.citation: Quadros, Francisco Raimundo Ewerton. 1892. Memoria sobre os trabalhos de exploração e observação efetuada pela secção da comissão militar encarregada da linha telegráfica de Uberaba a Cuiabá, de fevereiro a junho de 1889. Revista do Instituto Histórico e Geográfico Brasileiro 55(1):233-260.
new_statements.locator: p. 255 (end of the section on the 'Xavantes' of São Paulo, immediately before the Vocabulario Comparado, pp. 256-259); quoted verbatim in Baldus 1954: 82
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: QUOTE: Opened (page scan of p. 25 = printed p. 255 of; the PDF itself has no text beyond the etnolinguistica cover sheet). The passage is there word for word: 'Os Xavantes repellem a poligamia, e não empregam suas armas contra o homem. / Quando quazi todas as palavras de vocabulario dos Caiuás e dos Coroados terminam por silabas agudas, as dos xavantes têm quazi todas o acento agudo na penultima. / Resta-me aprezentar um rezumido vocabulario comparado d'essas trez linguas, com os termos correspondentes do guarani e do portuguez.' The only difference from the report's quote is that the original sets these as three separate paragraphs; wording, spelling (quazi, aprezentar, rezumido, trez) and…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent in Oti falls on the penultimate syllable in almost all words, in contrast to the final stress of neighbouring Guarani (Kaiowá) and Kaingang; an impressionistic observation by the collector of a ~50-item wordlist (1889), whose transcriptions mark the accent accordingly (Inuáde, Atáve, Guiáde, Tuásia, Catiága, Folháhe, Concéde).
new_statements.exceptions: Only the hedge 'quazi todas' (almost all); Quadros's own list has at least one final-accented form (Achô 'fire'). Not mentioned by Quadros but relevant: Nimuendajú's independent Oti list (in Ihering 1912: 255-260) writes the accent on the final syllable in many items (koaká, daká, kakí, iská, fugidó, kōsidé, gna'atá, otí), so the penult generalisation is not secure.
new_statements.domain_note: Isolated citation forms elicited from a wordlist; no word/phrase distinction possible. The language is extinct and attested only by ~110 words, so no fuller description can ever exist.
new_statements.identity_note: Quadros (1892) calls the group 'Xavantes' (of the São Paulo sertão, = Curuton of the Coroados, Oto of the Guarani); this is the Oti of Campos Novos / Paranapanema (otii1244), not the Akwẽ-Xavante of Mato Grosso (xava1240) nor the Ofayé-'Chavante' (ofay1240). Ihering (1895, 1904) and Baldus (1954: 82) explicitly identify Quadros's 'Xavante' vocabulary as Oti. The language is extinct; the entire corpus is ~110 words in three wordlists (Quadros 1892, Borba 1908, Nimuendajú in Ihering 1912).

new_statements.quote: Os Chavantes do Estado de S. Paulo, que vivem no curso inferior dos rios Tieté e Paranapanema, são muito differentes dos Caingangs, e sua lingua se distingue bem tanto da dos Caingangs como da dos Chavantes do Matto Grosso. Por essa razão denominei-os Eochavantes. Possuimos dous vocabularios de sua lingua; um que foi publicado pelo General Ewerton Quadros (N.º 12) e outro por Telemaco Borba (N.º 7). [...] Como os dous vocabularios mencionados são pouco conhecidos darei no seguinte uma reproducção.
new_statements.translation: The Chavantes of the State of S. Paulo, who live on the lower course of the Tietê and Paranapanema rivers, are very different from the Caingangs, and their language is clearly distinct both from that of the Caingangs and from that of the Chavantes of Matto Grosso. For that reason I named them Eochavantes. We possess two vocabularies of their language; one published by General Ewerton Quadros (No. 12) and the other by Telemaco Borba (No. 7). [...] Since the two vocabularies mentioned are little known I give a reproduction of them below.
new_statements.citation: Ihering, Hermann von. 1907. A anthropologia do estado de São Paulo. Revista do Museu Paulista 7:202-257 (comparative Eochavante vocabulary from Borba and Quadros, pp. 228-231); also Ihering 1904/1906 'The Anthropology of the State of S. Paulo, Brazil'.

Como os dous vocabularios mencionados s%o pouco conhecidos darei no seguinte uma reproduccio' (scanned noise only). pp. 228-231 are the Borba/Quadros table and p. 231-232 the Caingang/Tupi commentary, as the compiler says. BUT the compiler only scanned PDF pages 25-33 and declared the whole article silent. I scanned the rest (PDF pages 2-24 and 34-59, saved as ocr1907/p-02.p-24 and) and the ethnographi…
new_statements.relation_note: Silent in prose. The accent marks in the reproduced Quadros column are the same data behind the catalog's penult record (Quadros 1892), so nothing new; the work does not paraphrase Quadros's accent remark the way Ihering 1904 does.
new_statements.rule_in_words: No statement on accent or stress. The pages reproduce the Quadros and Borba word lists side by side; the Quadros column keeps acute accent marks on some forms (e.g. p. 231 Iustúa 'caixa', Iquéce 'dedo', Eféga 'tatú'), which are penultimate in those forms, but Ihering makes no remark about them. The commentary after the table (pp. 231-232) discusses Caingang 'tatá' and Tupi/Tapuya suffixes, not Eochavante prosody.
new_statements.identity_note: All three works concern the Oti of the lower Paranapanema-Tietê region of São Paulo, called 'Chavantes' in the 1890s-1900s sources and renamed 'Eochavantes' by Ihering (1904 p. 9-10; 1907 p. 227) to separate them from the Jê Xavante of Goiás/Mato Grosso. The Glottolog name 'Xavantes' for otii1244 refers to this São Paulo group, not to the Jê language xava1240. Nimuendajú's piece concerns the last Oti at Campos Novos do Paranapanema (1909-1910).
